label: copy phase: fed-back j (mid-sequence), strongest when next output is j or b
explanation: Fires only in the copy phase, and only when the token fed back in is j (100% of activations have in_tok == j). It never fires in the original or delimiter phases, or on any other input token. Within copy-phase j inputs it is selective: about 10% of them fire, mostly at recall_idx 3-4 (the j came from original positions 2-3), and almost never at recall_idx <= 2. The output at the current step sets the magnitude. The strongest activations are j followed by j or b (j j b patterns, e.g. h y w j j b ... -> top act at the first copied j). Other next tokens (k, 0, e, u, a, ...) give weak activations. The predicate (j input, recall_idx >= 3, out j/b) has high precision (~0.84) but captures only ~56% of the mass. Weak firings on j followed by other tokens make up the rest, and many such steps do not fire at all, so recall is incomplete.

scorecard.summary: Graded preference over the current input token (most: j, -, m, b, l, h; least: 1, 0, a, <DEL>) and the token being output (most: j, b, 0, k, u, e; least: 1, q, -, x); timing cues that raise it most: recall_idx=3, recall_idx=4, L=4 & t=6.
